10.1021_acs.estlett.6c00673: Precise ion–ion separation using nanofiltration (NF) membranes remains a central challenge in water treatment and resource recovery. Conventional fabrication by interfacial polymerization (IP) provides limited control over the structure of the polyamide (PA) selective layer, thereby constraining ion–ion separation. Using a solvent-free, vapor-phase, layer-by-layer approach, we synthesized a PA selective layer for NF via molecular layer deposition (MLD) of trimesoyl chloride (TMC) and piperazine (PIP). This strategy enables angstrom-scale control over PA growth with a deposition rate of 1.3 Å per cycle and yields spatially uniform membranes with a mean pore size of 5.08 Å and a narrow geometric standard deviation of 1.18. MLD further enables precise control over surface chemistry through either TMC or PIP termination. Structural, chemical, and transport characterizations indicate an enhanced size-based exclusion and reduced Donnan exclusion in the MLD-grown membranes. MLD membranes with ∼39 nm-thick PA layer exhibited a water permeance of 13.0 L m–2 h–1 bar–1 and monovalent–divalent cation (Li+/Mg2+) and anion (Cl–/SO42–) selectivities of 36 and 92, respectively. This work establishes MLD-grown PA membranes as a model platform for precise PA structural control and mechanistic interrogation of ion–ion separation, providing design principles for more selective membranes.
10.1021_acs.nanolett.5c06238: High-temperature solid oxide electrolysis cells (SOECs) offer a promising pathway for CO 2 -to-CO conversion yet are hindered by cathode inactivity. This study demonstrates cation doping in Sr 2 Ti 0.8 Fe 1.2 O 6−δ (STF), specifically forming Sr 2 Ti 0.8 FeNi 0.2 O 6−δ (STFN) and Sr 2 Ti 0.8 FeCo 0.2 O 6−δ (STFC), as an effective strategy for modulating oxygen activity and enhancing CO 2 electrolysis performance. The STFC cathode delivers optimal results, achieving a 1.15 A cm –2 current density, 8.01 mL min –1 cm –2 CO production rate, and >99% Faradaic efficiency at 1.6 V and 800 °C. Advanced spectroscopic techniques combined with density functional theory calculations reveal that Co doping increases oxygen activity, evidenced by an upshifted O 2p band center and reduced oxygen vacancy formation energy. Consequently, CO 2 adsorption for carbonate (CO 3 2– ) intermediate formation is facilitated, and the energy barrier for CO generation is reduced. A techno-economic assessment projects a competitive CO production cost of $748 per ton. These insights provide fundamental guidelines for the design of high-activity catalysts in high-temperature electrochemical systems.
10.1109_tsg.2026.3668122: Photovoltaic (PV) power plant variability presents a significant obstacle to grid stability. Hybrid energy storage systems (HESSs), which integrate battery energy storage systems (BESSs) with hydrogen units (i.e., electrolyzers and fuel cells), offer a viable solution to mitigate PV fluctuations and minimize power curtailment. However, existing control strategies are typically rule-based or offline-optimized, lacking the capability to address critical real-time challenges such as nonlinear efficiency characteristics, response delays in hydrogen subsystems, excessive hydrogen consumption, and battery degradation while complying with grid codes. This paper introduces an adaptive Equivalent Consumption Minimization Strategy (ECMS) for real-time, optimal power sharing among hydrogen-BESS systems. The controller minimizes a composite cost function that integrates efficiency-aware dispatch using empirical efficiency curves, health-aware penalties for aggressive state-of-charge (SOC) reversals and hydrogen overuse, delay-resilient compensation for hydrogen subsystem response lags, and degradation-aware control via online BESS aging assessment. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed strategy significantly improves ramp rate (RR) compliance and system longevity. Compared to benchmark techniques, the ECMS reduces BESS degradation by 50% and nearly eliminates RR violations while maintaining hydrogen demand satisfaction and ensuring smooth SOC recovery.
10.1186_s12951-025-03892-z: Spermatozoa exit the testis in an immotile and immature state, and obtain motility and maturity in the epididymis with the most abundant functions acquired in its initial segment (IS). The reshaping of polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs) exposure on the epididymis, however, has never been studied in detail yet, let alone from a multi-omic perspective. Herein, we utilized single-cell transcriptomics, untargeted metabolomics and in vivo experiments to explore PS-NPs-induced cellular remodeling of rat IS. A dose-dependent decrease in the epithelial thickness was merely observed in the IS (Control vs. low vs. medium vs. high group, 38.33 ± 2.52 vs. 32.67 ± 3.15 vs. 21.67 ± 3.58 vs. 11.08 ± 1.67 μm, respectively; P < 0.001) instead of the other three epididymal segments. PS-NPs exposure inhibited the acidification of epididymal luminal fluid (Control vs. low vs. medium vs. high group, pH, 6.05 ± 0.19 vs. 6.35 ± 0.14 vs. 6.57 ± 0.23 vs. 6.70 ± 0.24, respectively; P < 0.001), downregulated sperm acrosome reaction (Control vs. low vs. medium vs. high group, 42.67 ± 4.62% vs. 36.38 ± 4.04% vs. 28.07 ± 3.46% vs. 17.69 ± 2.52%, respectively; P < 0.05), and reduced sperm motility (Control vs. low vs. medium vs. high group, 83.08 ± 4.02% vs. 76.33 ± 2.08% vs. 70.67 ± 3.79% vs. 65.33 ± 2.89%, respectively; P < 0.01). Cell apoptosis after exposure existed across the IS without cell type-specificity. Besides, we found altered metabolic landscape and dysregulatory amino acid metabolites after exposure. Interestingly, cell-cell communication together with pseudotime trajectory delineated that PS-NPs facilitated NK cell differentiation towards cytotoxic and proliferative subtypes, during which ICAM and TNF signalings were upregulated. Moreover, PS-NPs exposure upregulated AQP9 through activating ERK1/2 in principal cells. Furthermore, we observed dysfunctions and ultrastructural defects of blood-epididymal barrier with downregulated protein levels of tight junction (VIM, SOX9, KRT5 and β-catenin) and upregulated ROS levels in basal cells. In summary, we offer previously unidentified insights into the contribution of PS-NPs in epididymal IS and extend on existing knowledge of environmental contaminant-induced epididymis damage that merits future investigation.
